before.quote:
A **symplectic form** on a smooth manifold $M$ is a smooth two-form $\omega$
such that

1. $d\omega=0$, and
2. $(T_pM,\omega_p)$ is a [[def-symplectic-vector-space|symplectic vector
   space]] for every $p\in M$.

pointwise nondegeneracy are required. A zero-dimensional manifold with its
zero two-form satisfies the definition.

before.claim: On each closed ball, $T_z(Z)=z+(h/2)F(Z)$ maps the ball into itself because $\|T_z(Z)-z\|\le |h|M/2\le\rho$. The mean-value estimate on the convex ball gives $\|T_z(Z)-T_z(W)\|\le q\|Z-W\|$ with $q=|h|L_0/2<1$. The ball is complete, so [F1] gives a unique fixed point $Z$ and the stated convergent iteration.

Set $G(z,Z)=Z-z-(h/2)F(Z)$. At the selected branch, $D_ZG=I-(h/2)A$ with $A=DF(Z)$. Since $\|(h/2)A\|<1$, its inverse is the convergent Neumann series; [F2] therefore makes $Z$ a local $C^1$ function of $z$. Differentiating $G=0$ gives $D_zZ=(I-(h/2)A)^{-1}$ and hence $S:=D\Psi_h=(I-B)^{-1}(I+B),\qquad B=(h/2)A.$
By [F5], $A=J\nabla^2H(Z)$ and $A^TJ+JA=0$; therefore $B^TJ+JB=0$. Expanding both products gives $(I+B)^TJ(I+B)-(I-B)^TJ(I-B)=2(B^TJ+JB)=0$. Thus $(I-B)^TJ(I-B)=(I+B)^TJ(I+B)$.

The fixed-point equation and [F4] give $Z=z+(h/2)F(z)+(h^2/4)DF(z)F(z)+O(h^3)$ uniformly on the tube: first $Z-z=O(h)$ by the ball bound, then Taylor-expand $F(Z)$ at $z$ and substitute once. Consequently $2Z-z=z+hF(z)+(h^2/2)DF(z)F(z)+O(h^3)$. The exact flow has the same expansion by [F3], [F4], and [F6], so its one-step defect is at most $Ch^3$.

The matrices $I-B$ and $I+B$ commute. Multiplying the equality in step 1.3 on the left by $(I-B)^{-T}$ and on the right by $(I-B)^{-1}$ yields $J=(I-B)^{-T}(I+B)^TJ(I+B)(I-B)^{-1}=S^TJS$. This proves the exact branch is symplectic.

Differentiating the fixed-point relation shows $D\Psi_h=I+hDF(z)+O(h^2)$ uniformly on the tube; bounded derivatives make $\|D\Psi_h\|\le1+L_1h$ after decreasing $h_0$. The mean-value theorem on the stipulated convex comparison segments gives $e_{n+1}\le(1+L_1h)e_n+Ch^3$. Iteration and $(1+L_1h)^n\le e^{L_1T}$ give $e_n\le e^{L_1T}e_0+CTe^{L_1T}h^2$.
Steps 1.1–2.2 prove the unique admitted branch, symplecticity, local second order, and the stated finite-time error.

after.claim: Since $H\in C^2(U)$, the coordinate field $F$ is $C^1$. On the admitted closed ball, $T_z(W)=z+(h/2)F(W)$ maps the ball into itself because $\|T_z(W)-z\|\le |h|M/2\le\rho$. The mean-value estimate on this convex ball gives $\|T_z(W)-T_z(V)\|\le\theta\|W-V\|$ with $\theta=|h|L/2<1$. The ball is nonempty and complete, so [F1] gives a unique fixed point $Z$, keeps all iterates in the ball, and gives $\|Z_k-Z\|\le b_k=\theta^k\|Z_1-Z_0\|/(1-\theta)$. Multiplication by two gives $\|(2Z_k-z)-(2Z-z)\|=2\|Z_k-Z\|\le2b_k$, and $Z\in\overline B(z,\rho)$ gives $\|(2Z-z)-z\|\le2\rho$. The convention $\theta^0=1$ makes the bound valid at $k=0$. If $\theta=0$, $T_z$ is constant on the ball, hence $Z_1=T_z(z)=T_z(Z)=Z$ and every later iterate equals $Z$; thus $b_k=0$ for $k\ge1$. These assertions require only the $C^2$ hypotheses.

For the remaining claims, assume the additional $C^3$ and uniform branch hypotheses. Fix an admitted initial value $z$ and let $z_j\to z$ through admitted initial values with selected roots $Z_j$. Since $\|Z_j-z_j\|\le\rho$, the sequence is bounded; every convergent subsequence has a limit $Z_*\in\overline B(z,\rho)\subset U$, and continuity of $F$ in $Z_j=z_j+(h/2)F(Z_j)$ shows $Z_*=z+(h/2)F(Z_*)$. The contraction in step 1.1 gives uniqueness of this fixed point in $\overline B(z,\rho)$, so every convergent subsequence has limit $Z$ and therefore $Z_j\to Z$. Now put $G(z,Z)=Z-z-(h/2)F(Z)$. At the selected root, $D_ZG=I-(h/2)A$ with $A=DF(Z)$. Since $\|(h/2)A\|<1$, this matrix is invertible by the Neumann series, and [F2] supplies a local $C^1$ root branch. The continuity just proved and the IFT's local uniqueness identify the selected roots with this branch at every nearby admitted initial value. Differentiating $G=0$ gives $D_zZ=(I-(h/2)A)^{-1}$ and hence $S:=D\Psi_h=(I-B)^{-1}(I+B),\qquad B=(h/2)A.$

Put $m=2d$ and $\delta=Z-z$. The admitted fixed-point equation gives $\|\delta\|\le |h|\|F(Z)\|/2\le |h|M/2$, hence $\delta=O(|h|)$ uniformly. Since $H\in C^3$, $F\in C^2$. Apply the scalar theorem [F4] to each $F_i$ along $[z,Z]$: $F_i(z+\delta)=F_i(z)+DF_i(z)\delta+R_i$, where $R_i=\tfrac12D^2F_i(z+\vartheta_i\delta)[\delta,\delta]$ for some $\vartheta_i\in(0,1)$. These points may differ with $i$. Bounded second derivatives on the tube give $|R_i|\le C_i\|\delta\|^2$, hence $\|R\|_2\le(\sum_{i=1}^m C_i^2)^{1/2}\|\delta\|^2$. Substitution into $\delta=(h/2)F(z+\delta)$ first gives $\delta=(h/2)F(z)+O(h^2)$ and then $\delta=(h/2)F(z)+(h^2/4)DF(z)F(z)+O(|h|^3)$. Thus $2Z-z=z+hF(z)+(h^2/2)DF(z)F(z)+O(|h|^3)$. For the exact flow, write $g_i(t)=(\varphi_t(z))_i$. By [F3] and [F6], $g_i^{(1)}=F_i(\varphi_t(z))$, $g_i^{(2)}=DF_i(\varphi_t(z))F(\varphi_t(z))$, and $g_i^{(3)}=D^2F_i(\varphi_t(z))[F(\varphi_t(z)),F(\varphi_t(z))]+DF_i(\varphi_t(z))DF(\varphi_t(z))F(\varphi_t(z))$ are defined, with the third derivative uniformly bounded on the controlled trajectories. Scalar Taylor in time gives $g_i(h)=z_i+hF_i(z)+(h^2/2)(DF(z)F(z))_i+(h^3/6)g_i^{(3)}(\eta_i h)$ for $h\ne0$, with possibly distinct $\eta_i\in(0,1)$. Each last term is bounded by $C_i'|h|^3$; summing their squares gives a Euclidean remainder bound $(\sum_{i=1}^m(C_i')^2)^{1/2}|h|^3$. The case $h=0$ is immediate. The exact flow therefore has the same terms through degree two as $2Z-z$, giving the uniform one-step defect $C|h|^3$ for either sign of $h$. No common Lagrange intermediate point for the vector is used.
By [F5], $A=J\nabla^2H(Z)$ and $A^TJ+JA=0$; therefore $B^TJ+JB=0$. Expanding both products gives $(I+B)^TJ(I+B)-(I-B)^TJ(I-B)=2(B^TJ+JB)=0$. Thus $(I-B)^TJ(I-B)=(I+B)^TJ(I+B)$.

Differentiating the fixed-point relation shows $D\Psi_h=I+hDF(z)+O(h^2)$ uniformly on the tube; bounded derivatives make $\|D\Psi_h\|\le1+L_1|h|$ after decreasing $h_0$. The mean-value theorem on the stipulated convex comparison segments gives $e_{n+1}\le(1+L_1|h|)e_n+C|h|^3$. Iteration and $(1+L_1|h|)^n\le e^{L_1T}$ when $n|h|\le T$ give $e_n\le e^{L_1T}e_0+CTe^{L_1T}|h|^2$.

The matrices $I-B$ and $I+B$ commute. Multiplying the equality in step 3.1 on the left by $(I-B)^{-T}$ and on the right by $(I-B)^{-1}$ yields $J=(I-B)^{-T}(I+B)^TJ(I+B)(I-B)^{-1}=S^TJS$. This proves the exact branch is symplectic.

Step 1.1 proves existence, uniqueness, convergence, and the stage and output certificates under the $C^2$ hypotheses. Under the additional $C^3$ and tube hypotheses, step 2.1 proves the exact branch's stated regularity, step 4.1 proves symplecticity, and steps 2.2 and 3.2 prove local second order and the finite-time error.

$d(f(u),f(v)) \le q\,d(u,v)$ for all $u,v \in X$ and $0 \le q < 1$
([[def-lipschitz-holder-contraction]]). Then:

1. There is exactly one $x^{*} \in X$ with $f(x^{*}) = x^{*}$.
2. For every $x_0 \in X$ the sequence of **iterates**, defined by recursion
   ([[thm-recursion]]) by $x_{n+1} := f(x_n)$, converges to $x^{*}$ in $(X,d)$

   with the integer power of [[def-integer-power]].

$$F(q,p):=\bigl(\nabla_pH(q,p),-\nabla_qH(q,p)\bigr)=J\nabla H(q,p).$$
Given $z\in U$, for a signed step $h$, the **exact local implicit midpoint step** is defined by
$$Z=z+\frac h2F(Z),\qquad z^+=2Z-z,$$
using the locally unique solution $Z$ in a declared closed ball $\overline B(z,\rho)\subset U$. The branch is admissible when certified bounds $M\ge\sup_{\overline B}\|F\|$ and $L\ge\sup_{\overline B}\|DF\|$ satisfy $|h|M/2\le\rho$ and $|h|L/2<1$. For a finite iteration implementation of these exact operations, input an output tolerance $\tau>0$ and an update budget $B\in\mathbb N_0$. Use $\theta=|h|L/2$ and proceed as follows.

1. Set $Z_0=z$. If $B=0$, return `inconclusive` with current stage iterate $Z_0$, approximate output $z$, and output-error bound $2\rho$.
2. If $B\ge1$, compute $Z_1=z+(h/2)F(Z_0)$ and set $d_1=\|Z_1-Z_0\|$.
3. For $k=1,\ldots,B$, set $b_k=\theta^k d_1/(1-\theta)$ and the output radius $r_k=2b_k$. If $r_k\le\tau$, return the approximation $2Z_k-z$ with output-error certificate $r_k$. Otherwise, if $k<B$, compute $Z_{k+1}=z+(h/2)F(Z_k)$ and continue. If the check fails at $k=B$, return `inconclusive` with current stage iterate $Z_B$, approximate output $2Z_B-z$, and output-error bound $2b_B$.

When $\theta=0$, use $\theta^k=0$ for $k\ge1$; the procedure never evaluates $0^0$. $$Z=z+\frac h2F(Z),\qquad z^+=2Z-z,$$
using the locally unique solution $Z$ in a declared closed ball $\overline B(z,\rho)\subset U$. The branch is admissible when certified bounds $M\ge\sup_{\overline B}\|F\|$ and $L\ge\sup_{\overline B}\|DF\|$ satisfy $|h|M/2\le\rho$ and $|h|L/2<1$. It returns `branch-not-certified` if the ball or bounds are unavailable, and `domain-failure` if the admitted ball is not contained in $U$.

For a finite implementation, start with $Z_0=z$ and iterate $Z_{k+1}=z+(h/2)F(Z_k)$ up to the supplied budget. The contraction estimate gives a certified radius for $Z_k-Z$. Return the approximation $2Z_k-z$ with that radius if it is within the requested tolerance; otherwise return `inconclusive` with the current iterate and bound. An approximate result is not asserted to be exactly symplectic. The exact map is the selected branch value $2Z-z$.

Let $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open, $V\in C^3(Q)$, and $M$ symmetric positive definite. Set $H(q,p)=\tfrac12p^TM^{-1}p+V(q)$ and $F(q,p)=(M^{-1}p,-\nabla V(q))$. Fix $T>0$ and $h=T/N$ with $N\ge1$. Suppose the exact solution, numerical states, all kick/drift intermediate states, and every line segment used below lie in one compact convex tube $K\Subset Q\times\mathbb R^d$, with the derivatives of $F$ through order two bounded there. For $z_0$ in that tube, write $e_n^E$ for the error of iterated kick-then-drift symplectic Euler and $e_n^V$ for the error of iterated local leapfrog relative to the exact solution at $t_n=nh$. For sufficiently small $h$, constants $C_E,C_V,L$ independent of $h,N,n$ satisfy, whenever $nh\le T$,
$$e_n^E\le e^{LT}e_0+C_ETe^{LT}h,\qquad e_n^V\le e^{LT}e_0+C_VTe^{LT}h^2.$$
Thus symplectic Euler has global order one and leapfrog has global order two on the stated controlled tube. No unconditional domain-admissibility claim is made.

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{2d}$ be open, $H\in C^3(U)$, and $F=J\nabla H$. Suppose, uniformly for initial values $z$ in a compact convex tube, that $\overline B(z,\rho)\subset U$, $\|F\|\le M$, $\|DF\|\le L_0$ on these balls, and $|h|M/2\le\rho$, $|h|L_0/2<1$. The exact implicit midpoint branch [[alg-implicit-midpoint-hamiltonian-step]] then exists uniquely in each ball. Its local map $\Psi_h(z)=2Z-z$ is $C^1$ and satisfies $D\Psi_h(z)^TJ D\Psi_h(z)=J$.

Assume also that the exact and numerical trajectories, the branch balls, and the segments used in comparison lie in a compact convex subset of $U$ for $nh\le T$, with the displayed derivatives uniformly bounded. Then for some constants $C,L_1$ independent of $h,n$,
$$\|\Psi_h(z)-\varphi_h(z)\|\le Ch^3,\qquad e_n\le e^{L_1T}e_0+CTe^{L_1T}h^2,$$
where $\varphi_h$ is the exact Hamiltonian flow and $e_n=\|z_n-\varphi_{nh}(z_0)\|$.

Let $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be open and star-shaped about a point $q_*\in Q$, meaning $q_*+t(q-q_*)\in Q$ for every $q\in Q$ and $t\in[0,1]$. Let $M$ be real symmetric positive-definite, $U=Q\times\mathbb R^d$, and equip $U$ with the canonical form $\omega=\sum_{i=1}^d dq_i\wedge dp_i$ and matrix $J=\begin{pmatrix}0&I\\-I&0\end{pmatrix}$. Set $H(q,p)=\tfrac12p^TM^{-1}p+V(q)$ with $V\in C^\infty(Q)$. Let $\Phi_h$ be the kick-then-drift symplectic-Euler map, the local leapfrog map, or an admitted implicit-midpoint branch, on a compact subset where the chosen map is defined. Write $r=1$ for the kick-then-drift symplectic-Euler map and $r=2$ for leapfrog or implicit midpoint, as proved in [[thm-local-symplectic-euler-and-leapfrog-trajectory-errors]] and [[thm-implicit-midpoint-branch-symplectic-order-and-error]]. For a smooth test function $f$, define the pullback $P_hf=f\circ\Phi_h$ by its Taylor coefficients at $h=0$. For fixed finite $N\ge r$, its truncated logarithm is the polynomial
$$\log_N(P_h)=\sum_{k=1}^{N+1}\frac{(-1)^{k+1}}{k}(P_h-I)^k,$$
computed modulo terms of order $h^{N+2}$. There are smooth vector fields $X_r,\ldots,X_N$ and globally defined functions $H_r,\ldots,H_N$ on $U$ such that
$$h^{-1}\log_N(P_h)=\mathcal L_{X_H}+\sum_{j=r}^Nh^j\mathcal L_{X_j}\pmod{h^{N+1}},\qquad \iota_{X_j}\omega=dH_j,$$
where $\mathcal L_Xf:=Df[X]$. Thus $H_h^{[N]}=H+\sum_{j=r}^Nh^jH_j$ is a globally defined finite modified Hamiltonian. The logarithm is a finite formal polynomial for each fixed $N$; no convergence of an infinite series is asserted.

Let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^{2d}$ be open, $H\in C^2(U)$, $z=(q,p)$, and $J=\begin{pmatrix}0&I\\-I&0\end{pmatrix}$; define $F(q,p)=(\nabla_pH(q,p),-\nabla_qH(q,p))=J\nabla H(q,p)$. For a signed step $h$, suppose a declared closed ball $\overline B(z,\rho)\subset U$ has bounds $\|F\|\le M$ and $\|DF\|\le L$ satisfying $|h|M/2\le\rho$ and $\theta:=|h|L/2<1$. The exact implicit midpoint branch [[alg-implicit-midpoint-hamiltonian-step]] then has a unique stage root $Z$ in this ball. The exact iterates $Z_0=z$, $Z_{k+1}=z+(h/2)F(Z_k)$ stay in the ball, converge to $Z$, and for every $k\in\mathbb N_0$ satisfy
$$\|Z_k-Z\|\le b_k:=\frac{\theta^k\|Z_1-Z_0\|}{1-\theta},\qquad \|(2Z_k-z)-(2Z-z)\|\le2b_k.$$
Here $\theta^0=1$, including when $\theta=0$; if $\theta=0$, the first update equals $Z$ and $b_k=0$ for $k\ge1$. Also $\|(2Z-z)-z\|\le2\rho$, which supplies an output-error bound when no update is computed.

Assume additionally $H\in C^3(U)$ and that these ball hypotheses hold uniformly for initial values $z$ in a compact convex tube, with common $\rho,M,L$. At every admitted initial value the selected branch is locally the restriction of a $C^1$ solution branch, and its exact local map $\Psi_h(z)=2Z-z$ satisfies $D\Psi_h(z)^TJ D\Psi_h(z)=J$.

Under these additional $C^3$ and uniform branch hypotheses, assume also that the exact and numerical trajectories, the branch balls, and the segments used in comparison lie in a compact convex subset of $U$ whenever $n|h|\le T$, with the displayed derivatives uniformly bounded. Then for some constants $C,L_1$ independent of $h,n$,
$$\|\Psi_h(z)-\varphi_h(z)\|\le C|h|^3,\qquad e_n\le e^{L_1T}e_0+CTe^{L_1T}|h|^2,$$
where $\varphi_h$ is the exact Hamiltonian flow and $e_n=\|z_n-\varphi_{nh}(z_0)\|$. These symplecticity and trajectory-error conclusions concern the exact selected map; no such conclusion is asserted here for a finite iteration output.

after.claim: Since $V'(q)=q$, [F1] gives $p^+=p-hq$ and $q^+=q+h(p-hq)=(1-h^2)q+hp$, which is the displayed matrix.
